identity.purpose: Illustrate a prescribed fragment release and cloud stretching over the first three revolutions.

physics.model: Edition-owned elliptic Kepler propagation from Cartesian release states, evaluated directly at every displayed time.
physics.incomingGeometry: Two equal-weight circular bodies meet at [R+h,0,0]; velocity inclinations +55 and -35 degrees give perpendicular paths.
physics.sampleWeights: Equal representative weights, not physical masses or predicted fragment yield.
physics.randomAlgorithm: Mulberry32; uniform spherical directions from uniform z and azimuth, paired with opposite vectors.

releaseSpeedMPerSecond.distribution: Every kick has the selected magnitude relative to its family mean. No fitted breakup distribution.

physics.momentum: Equal-weight family means conserve total incoming linear momentum; paired kicks sum to zero.
physics.energy: Relative mean velocity contraction removes more kinetic energy than the kicks add throughout the allowed slider range.
physics.frame: Synthetic inertial Cartesian axes mapped to Three world (x,z,-y). Earth rotates about its polar axis at 7.292115e-5 rad/s, with arbitrary orientation at contact and no dated geographical claim.
physics.drawnEarth: Existing WGS84 ellipsoid and pinned Natural Earth geography. Experiment heights are above the spherical reference, distinct from WGS84 geodetic altitude.
excluded: NASA Standard Breakup Model or fitted size/mass/velocity distributions
Atmospheric drag, reentry and long-term decay
Oblateness / J2, third bodies and radiation pressure

presentation.label: AN INDICATIVE SIMULATION
presentation.clock: Elapsed seconds from contact; separate from all dated catalogue clocks.
presentation.guidedPace: 50 authored seconds: approach 8s; contact hold 2s; release to +3min over 8s; +3min to +30min over 10s; +30min to three original periods over 22s. Stops at the bound.
presentation.camera: Continuous close encounter to Earth composition over the first 15 model minutes; gestures hand over the camera and preserve physical time.
presentation.glyphs: Two diamonds before contact; 192 samples at/after contact, with no duplicate parent glyphs. Authored point sizes and direction arrow lengths.
presentation.slider: Pauses at the displayed time; changes kick magnitudes with fixed seed/directions; directly recomputes states and period ranges.
presentation.reducedMotion: Opening and replay stay paused. Later preference changes pause and never automatically restart.
presentation.navigation: Discover and cross-links distinguish the synthetic experiment from the retained catalogue chapter.

references.role: Primary reference for the two-body initial-state problem and elliptic Kepler equation; no SPICE code copied or runtime dependency.
Primary reference for Earth GM, reference radius and nominal rotation rate. Numerical constants only.

rights.model: Edition-owned MIT code and synthetic initial conditions; no satellite records or licensed breakup dataset acquired.
rights.geography: Existing audited Natural Earth public-domain geometry is unchanged.

validation.unit: Encounter geometry, circular closure, seeded replay, fixed paired kicks, momentum and kinetic energy at slider extrema, positive perigees, orbital energy/angular momentum on forward/reverse seeks. Independent Cartesian RK4 with 2-second steps agrees after three orbits within 0.1 m position and 1 mm/s velocity.
validation.browser: Guided hold/release/stop, seek/replay/spread, camera clock preservation, reduced motion, keyboard, model scrolling, portrait/landscape, /zenit/ assets, no external requests.
validation.interpretation: Numerical validation of this authored two-body experiment, not empirical validation of fragmentation physics or a historical event.
